messages:
meera: quick follow-up — we need a concrete decision on what the edge does when an in-flight streaming inference switches backends mid-request. two high-level options: 'splice' (try to transfer session/state transparently) vs 'client-resume' (force client reconnect + resume token). thoughts?

jason: splice feels risky. TLS + connection semantics + node-local kv cache make it hairy. also operational surface for bugs increases. :thinking:

dani: +1 on avoiding TCP splice. my preference is client-resume with a compact resume token that lets us replay up to last acked token on new backend. keeps proxy simple and auditable.

sasha: replaying is fine but for LLMs the KV cache rebuild cost is nontrivial. can we have an optional checkpoint fast-restore API on model hosts? backend could advertise checkpoint ids that the proxy can request when switching.

olivia: we've experimented with checkpoint restore in Dedicated — restore times vary a lot but for short histories it's ~30-80ms. larger seqs = seconds. security note: checkpoints must be tenant-scoped and encrypted (KMS).

pete: ops notes: whatever we pick we need per-client retry budgets and dedupe via idempotency keys. also traces must survive switchover (keep trace id across resume). add explicit error codes so clients can react: e.g. 409 RESUME_REQUIRED, 425 SESSION_EXPIRED.

deploy-bot: canary: edge-proxy v2.4.1 -> prod at 2026-04-09T15:12:00Z (no deploys blocked)

meera: proposed compromise: default = client-resume. require an X-Resume-Token header (opaque) that the client gets from first response chunk. proxy supports an opt-in fast-path: if backend reports a matching checkpoint id and 'fast-restore' true, proxy can request a hot restore and then forward without full replay. retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, max 2 backend-switch attempts per request, and propagate original trace id. also: proxy should surface clear metrics: switch_count, restore_latency, resume_replay_tokens. @jason @dani can you sketch RFC w/ state diagram?

jason: will do. include flowchart for: initial connect -> stream start -> backend fail -> proxy tries fast-restore -> fallback to resume replay -> final failure. also define header names and error codes.

dani: adding sample header snippet here:
```
X-Resume-Token: v1:tenant987:seq:1482:signature
X-Session-Trace: trace-9f3a
X-Retry-Budget: 2
```

meera: perfect. small todos: (1) add limits on replay window (N tokens) and max replay time budget (ms), (2) prove metrics don't regress pipeline SLOs, (3) security review for checkpoint export. I'll open RFC draft and ping infra for perf tests. :thumbsup:

sasha: one more: add a flag for customers to opt into 'best-effort fast-restore' vs 'strict replay-only' in tenant config. some customers will prefer determinism over speed.

pete: noted. also we should log an event when we switch backends with context: tenant, trace, switch_reason, checkpoint_id (if any). helps post-incident triage.

meera: thanks everyone — I'll create the RFC doc in /docs/arch and link here when ready.
